questions.question: In the allyl system (3 carbons, 3 p orbitals), what is the nodal structure of the non-bonding orbital (ψ₂)?

options.label: A
options.text: A spherical node surrounding the whole molecule.

options.label: B
options.text: Zero nodes across all three carbons.

options.label: C
options.text: Two nodes located between C1-C2 and C2-C3.

options.label: D
options.text: One vertical nodal plane passing directly through the central carbon atom (C2), leaving orbital lobes only on C1 and C3.

questions.correct_answer: One vertical nodal plane passing directly through the central carbon atom (C2), leaving orbital lobes only on C1 and C3.
questions.explanation: The ψ₂ non-bonding orbital of the allyl system has a node at C2; electron density in ψ₂ resides exclusively at the terminal carbons C1 and C3.

questions.topic: Allyl Cation vs Anion FMO Occupancy
questions.question: What is the HOMO of the allyl cation [C₃H₅⁺] compared to the allyl anion [C₃H₅⁻]?

options.label: A
options.text: Both have ψ₂ as the HOMO.

options.label: B
options.text: The cation has ψ₃* as the HOMO.

options.label: C
options.text: Both have ψ₁ as the HOMO.

options.label: D
options.text: The HOMO of the allyl cation is ψ₁ (2π electrons); the HOMO of the allyl anion is ψ₂ (4π electrons, non-bonding).

questions.correct_answer: The HOMO of the allyl cation is ψ₁ (2π electrons); the HOMO of the allyl anion is ψ₂ (4π electrons, non-bonding).
questions.explanation: The allyl cation has 2 π electrons filling ψ₁ (HOMO); the allyl anion has 4 π electrons filling ψ₁ and ψ₂ (HOMO).

questions.question: How many vertical nodes exist in each of the four π molecular orbitals of 1,3-butadiene (ψ₁ through ψ₄*)?

options.label: A
options.text: ψ₁ has 0 nodes, ψ₂ has 1 node (HOMO), ψ₃* has 2 nodes (LUMO), and ψ₄* has 3 nodes (all out-of-phase).

options.label: B
options.text: ψ₁ has 2 nodes, ψ₂ has 0 nodes.

options.label: C
options.text: All orbitals have 0 nodes.

options.label: D
options.text: ψ₁ has 1, ψ₂ has 2, ψ₃ has 3, ψ₄ has 4.

questions.correct_answer: ψ₁ has 0 nodes, ψ₂ has 1 node (HOMO), ψ₃* has 2 nodes (LUMO), and ψ₄* has 3 nodes (all out-of-phase).
questions.explanation: The number of vertical nodes in a linear conjugated polyene system equals (n - 1), where n is the orbital index.

questions.question: In 1,3-butadiene, what is the relative phase (sign) of the terminal p orbitals (C1 and C4) in the HOMO (ψ₂)?

options.label: A
options.text: Opposite phases (antisymmetric with respect to the mirror plane; symmetric with respect to C₂ inversion).

options.label: B
options.text: Zero coefficient on both terminal carbons.

options.label: C
options.text: Both terminal lobes are non-bonding.

options.label: D
options.text: Identical phases (symmetric with respect to mirror plane).

questions.correct_answer: Opposite phases (antisymmetric with respect to the mirror plane; symmetric with respect to C₂ inversion).
questions.explanation: The HOMO (ψ₂) of butadiene has 1 central node, giving opposite phases at the C1 and C4 terminal lobes.

questions.question: In 1,3-butadiene, what is the relative phase of the terminal p orbitals (C1 and C4) in the LUMO (ψ₃*)?

options.label: A
options.text: Negative charge on all four lobes.

options.label: B
options.text: Identical phases (symmetric with respect to the mirror plane perpendicular to the C2-C3 bond).

options.label: C
options.text: Zero amplitude at terminal carbons.

options.label: D
options.text: Opposite phases.

questions.correct_answer: Identical phases (symmetric with respect to the mirror plane perpendicular to the C2-C3 bond).
questions.explanation: The LUMO (ψ₃*) has 2 nodes (between C1-C2 and C3-C4), resulting in identical in-phase signs at C1 and C4.

questions.question: In the electronic structure of ozone (O₃), how are the 4 π electrons distributed across the three oxygen atoms?

options.label: A
options.text: Two electrons in the bonding ψ₁ MO and two electrons in the non-bonding ψ₂ MO with nodes on the central oxygen, leaving terminal oxygens with partial charges.

options.label: B
options.text: Two electrons in ψ₃* antibonding orbital.

options.label: C
options.text: Four electrons in localized single bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: All four electrons in non-bonding d orbitals.

questions.correct_answer: Two electrons in the bonding ψ₁ MO and two electrons in the non-bonding ψ₂ MO with nodes on the central oxygen, leaving terminal oxygens with partial charges.
questions.explanation: Ozone is an isoelectronic 3-center 4-electron π system analogous to the allyl anion, with non-bonding electron density localized on terminal oxygens.

questions.question: In the benzyl radical (PhCH₂•), in which molecular orbital does the unpaired radical electron reside?

options.label: A
options.text: In the non-bonding Single Occupied Molecular Orbital (SOMO, ψ₄), with wave function amplitude distributed exclusively at the benzylic carbon and ortho/para ring carbons.

options.label: B
options.text: In the lowest energy bonding orbital ψ₁.

options.label: C
options.text: In the σ* antibonding orbital of the methyl group.

options.label: D
options.text: In the LUMO ψ₅*.

questions.correct_answer: In the non-bonding Single Occupied Molecular Orbital (SOMO, ψ₄), with wave function amplitude distributed exclusively at the benzylic carbon and ortho/para ring carbons.
questions.explanation: The SOMO of the benzyl radical has zero coefficients at meta carbons and non-zero amplitudes at the benzylic, ortho, and para positions.

questions.topic: Conjugation and Optical Band Gap Reduction
questions.question: How does extending π conjugation from ethylene (1 double bond) to 1,3,5-hexatriene (3 double bonds) affect the HOMO-LUMO energy gap (ΔE)?

options.label: A
options.text: The energy gap increases, shifting absorption to higher energy X-rays.

options.label: B
options.text: The energy gap remains completely unchanged.

options.label: C
options.text: The molecule becomes completely transparent.

options.label: D
options.text: The energy gap ΔE decreases systematically, shifting the electronic absorption (λmax) to longer wavelengths (bathochromic red shift).

questions.correct_answer: The energy gap ΔE decreases systematically, shifting the electronic absorption (λmax) to longer wavelengths (bathochromic red shift).
questions.explanation: As conjugation length increases, the spacing between MO levels decreases, narrowing ΔE = E_LUMO - E_HOMO and shifting absorption toward the visible spectrum.

questions.topic: Aromatic vs Antiaromatic Frost Circle Derivation
questions.question: Using a Frost Circle inscribed vertex-down in a circle of radius 2β, how many bonding MOs does planar cyclobutadiene (C₄H₄) have?

options.label: A
options.text: Four degenerate bonding MOs.

options.label: B
options.text: Two bonding and two antibonding MOs.

options.label: C
options.text: Three bonding MOs and one antibonding MO.

options.label: D
options.text: One bonding MO (lowest vertex), two degenerate non-bonding MOs (on the horizontal center line), and one antibonding MO.

questions.correct_answer: One bonding MO (lowest vertex), two degenerate non-bonding MOs (on the horizontal center line), and one antibonding MO.
questions.explanation: Inscribing a 4-membered ring vertex-down yields 1 bonding level, 2 degenerate non-bonding levels (containing 2 unpaired electrons = antiaromatic diradical), and 1 antibonding level.

questions.topic: Benzene Frost Circle Aromatic Closed Shell
questions.question: How does a Frost Circle for benzene (6-membered ring) demonstrate its closed-shell aromatic stability?

options.label: A
options.text: It shows an open-shell diradical configuration.

options.label: B
options.text: It places 1 lowest-energy bonding MO and 2 degenerate bonding MOs below the center line, completely filled by 6 π electrons with zero non-bonding or antibonding electrons.

options.label: C
options.text: It places all six electrons in antibonding orbitals.

options.label: D
options.text: It has three degenerate non-bonding orbitals.

questions.correct_answer: It places 1 lowest-energy bonding MO and 2 degenerate bonding MOs below the center line, completely filled by 6 π electrons with zero non-bonding or antibonding electrons.
questions.explanation: Benzene's Frost circle has 3 bonding MOs (all filled by 6 π electrons) forming a completely closed, exceptionally stable electronic shell.

questions.question: In 1,3-butadiene, what is the relative phase (sign) of the terminal p orbitals (C1 and C4) in the HOMO (ψ₂)?

questions.topic: Conjugation and Optical Band Gap Reduction
questions.question: How does extending π conjugation from ethylene (1 double bond) to 1,3,5-hexatriene (3 double bonds) affect the HOMO-LUMO energy gap (ΔE)?

options.text: The molecule becomes completely transparent.
